newsitem.title: CHINA: Two Koreas sign accord on 50,000 tonnes of food aid.
newsitem.headline: Two Koreas sign accord on 50,000 tonnes of food aid.

text.p: The two Red Cross Societies of rival North and South Korea signed an agreement on Friday to provide 50,000 tonnes of food aid to the hungry North, officials said.

"The North Korean side said they are satisfied with the amount," Lee Byoung-woong, secretary general of the South Korean Red Cross Society, told reporters after the signing of the agreement that followed three days of talks in Beijing.

The value of this second batch of aid was put at $10 million and the corn was to be delivered by the end of September, Lee said. "The two sides expressed hope for a good harvest in October and hoped this could be the last delivery," Lee said.
The aid would be delivered in three shipments by land and two by sea and most of the grain would come from China, South Korean officials said.

The North Korean side had also requested rice but this was turned down because of what the Southern side said was a lack of transparency offered by Pyongyang on the delivery of the grain to designated areas, Lee told reporters.

International aid workers say the communist North is on the brink of famine after floods in 1995 and 1996 devastated much of the country's farmland and industrial bases, exacerbating already severe food shortages.
